subject: discrete-mathematics
subtopics: graph vocabulary, degree and the handshake lemma
paths, cycles, connected components and the edge bounds n-k and C(n-k+1,2)
cut vertices, bridges, biconnected components and the two DFS criteria
vertex and edge connectivity, and the chain kappa <= lambda <= delta
Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs, including Dirac's sufficient condition
bipartite graphs, the odd-cycle criterion and the floor(n^2/4) edge bound
matching: maximal, maximum, perfect, and augmenting paths
Hall's marriage theorem and complete matching
vertex cover, independent set, clique and Koenig's theorem
chromatic number, greedy bounds, Brooks' theorem and the standard families
chromatic polynomial and counting proper colourings

chosen.title: Graph Theory: Connectivity, Coloring, Matching
covers: graph, simple graph, degree, complete graph, walk, path and circuit
Euler line and the all-even-degree criterion, Hamiltonian circuits and the degree n/2 sufficient condition
cut-set, cut-vertex, edge connectivity and vertex connectivity, with the two upper bounds
chromatic number, chromatic partitioning, the cycle and complete-graph values, bipartite as 2-chromatic
independent set, the n/k bound and the matching vocabulary
complete matching and the r-subset form of Hall's theorem
chosen.why: The only GATE-oriented source found whose text matches this syllabus line word for word - its title is the syllabus line - and whose pages could actually be read in this run. It states the definitions in the vocabulary GATE uses, gives the counterexamples the exam reuses, and its later pages cover matching and Hall. Chosen for fit and readability, not for size. The fetch was truncated after the Havel-Hakimi example, so the matching pages were read only as excerpts, which is why the status is PARTIAL.

chosen.title: Graph Theory subject notes, Volume 1 chapter
covers: the GATE weightage table for this topic from 2010 to 2026
counting formulas: 2^(C(n,2)) labelled graphs, n^(n-2) spanning trees, adjacency-matrix path counts
BFS and DFS purposes, including bridges and articulation points
chosen.why: Used to confirm the subtopic enumeration against GATE's own question record and to check the counting formulas that border this topic. It was not used as a teaching source for any card claim: it is a compressed revision sheet that assumes the material. Read in part, because the fetch was truncated in the graph-algorithm section.

chosen.title: Discrete Mathematics, Graph Theory lectures 44-52: Graph Theory Basics, Matching, Proof of Hall's Marriage Theorem, Various Operations on Graphs, Vertex and Edge Connectivity, Euler Path and Euler Circuit, Hamiltonian Circuit, Vertex and Edge Coloring
covers: lecture 46 proof of Hall's marriage theorem
lecture 50 Euler path and Euler circuit
chosen.why: The published lecture sequence is the closest map of this topic in teaching order, and it was used to confirm that the eleven subtopics are complete rather than to source any statement. Recorded as structure only: the transcript PDFs could not be fetched in this run, so no card quotes or timestamps it.

standard_refs: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, ch. 10 (graphs, connectivity, Euler and Hamilton, colouring, chromatic polynomial)
West, Introduction to Graph Theory (Brooks' theorem, Dirac's theorem, Koenig's theorem, matching)
CLRS, ch. 22 problem 22-2 (articulation points and bridges by DFS) and ch. 26 (maximum bipartite matching as flow)
note: Every numeric, chromatic, matching and cover claim published in this topic is recomputed by check_graphs() in scripts/validate.py, including by exhaustive enumeration over every graph on up to 5 vertices. No source was quoted; each card paraphrases and then re-derives.
